title: Security Misconfiguration
brief: **Ticket:** the app ships without security headers. Identify the header that stops MIME sniffing.
theory:
## Security misconfiguration (OWASP A05)
Send security headers on every response: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Referrer-Policy`. Return generic errors; never run debug mode on a reachable server.
worked_example:
```
$ curl -s -D - https://good.example/ -o /dev/null | grep -i content-security
content-security-policy: default-src 'self'
```

knowledge_check.q: Error pages shown to users should be ___
Which header limits what scripts can load/run?

investigation.intro: Compare the headers the lab app sends in vulnerable vs secure mode.
steps:
```bash
cd /workspaces/examto/appsec-lab
python3 -m venv .venv 2>/dev/null; . .venv/bin/activate 2>/dev/null; pip install -q -r requirements.txt
python3 run_server.py               # leave this running
```

In a second terminal, look at the headers (vulnerable — note what's missing):
```bash
curl -s -D - http://127.0.0.1:5000/health -o /dev/null
```
Restart the app with `LAB_SECURE=1 python3 run_server.py` and look again — the security headers now appear. The one with value `nosniff` is your answer.
hints: Submit the header name, lowercase is fine.

capture.task: **Name the control.** Which response header (its name) carries the value `nosniff`?
